title: The Second Locked Door Opened on My 25th Birthday… (Part 2)
hook: Part 2: Behind the second locked door…
story: Behind the second locked door in my parents' house was a room full of letters from strangers. Hundreds of them. If you missed part one: on my eighteenth birthday, my parents showed me a basement full of every drawing I'd ever made. Then they told me there was a second door, and it would open when I turned twenty-five. Last week, I turned twenty-five. My mom handed me the key, and this time she was crying before I even touched the handle. The room was tiny. Just shelves, covered in envelopes. Every single one was addressed to me. My parents explained that every time I finished a drawing as a kid, they made a copy and mailed it to the children's hospital downtown. For years. And the kids wrote back. "Your dragon made me laugh after surgery." "I hung your rocket ship over my bed." I read letters until two in the morning. Then I found one with handwriting I knew. It was from a little girl named Lily, age nine, thanking me for a drawing of a cat in a space helmet. Lily is my art director now. She's the one who hired me at twenty-two. She never told me. And when I called her that night, she said just one thing: "I was wondering when you'd open the second door."
